Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this candidate must be grounded in the current multi-wake keyframes. I’ll read the workspace contract first, then the skill instructions and rollout evidence before touching the policy.

The evidence set has four rollouts but only two distinct scores, and the prefilled policy is slightly worse than the sampled terminal-unloading variant. I’m now separating true controller differences from duplicate evaluations and checking the visual claims against the tabulated trajectory/load data.

The visual evidence narrows this candidate sharply: all variants remain outside the useful wake corridor, actively swim upstream, then curl nose-up into the upper boundary. Partial gated anterior allocation (`0.10`) is the measured navigation anchor; both full anterior unload (`0.0`) and gated posterior attenuation (`0.55`) preserve the same exit while worsening travel and range. The skill therefore leads me to document an exact rollback to the strongest measured allocation before editing the policy.

The candidate and durable lesson are now updated. I’m invoking the required checker as specified: semantic guidance/provenance first, then the lightweight Julia contract test, then the editable-boundary audit—no CFD.

The first check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: the same assigned parent is marked twice on adjacent README lines, so the checker cannot resolve “exactly one” parent. I’m removing only that identical duplicate marker—without changing the task contract or parent identity—then rerunning the check.

The semantic guidance check and solver-boundary audit pass. The Julia contract command cannot run because this worker image has no `julia` executable, so I’m completing the deterministic schema/prohibited-signal checks statically and verifying the policy delta against both the prefill and strongest sampled controller.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 target-policy candidate.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:18) restores the strongest measured `0.10/0.65` terminal joint allocation.
- [Visual diagnosis and hypothesis](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records the evidence and falsification boundaries.
- [Reusable guidance](guidance/control_experience.md:126) now brackets full anterior and posterior attenuation as negative continuations.
- Removed one identical duplicate assigned-parent marker from [README.md](README.md:452), allowing the required checker to resolve the unchanged parent.

Guidance and boundary checks pass. Static parameter-schema and prohibited-signal audits pass. The Julia contract command was invoked but could not run because Julia is unavailable. No CFD was run.
